unit.title: Install distribution panels, metering sockets, terminal mains and meter earthing systems

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is the usual mains supply to a home in Jamaica?
options: 110 V and 220 V, single-phase
110 V only, direct current (DC)
240 V and 415 V, three-phase
12 V and 24 V, single-phase

questions.stem: In a 110 V / 220 V single-phase supply, where do you get 220 V for a water heater?
options: Between one line and the neutral bar
Between the neutral bar and the earth bar
Between the two line (live) conductors
Between one line and the earth rod

questions.stem: Who is allowed to connect the supply to a new meter socket and fit the meter?
options: Any electrician who has finished the wiring
Only the power company, after approval
The customer, once the panel is installed
Any trainee, under an instructor's eye

questions.stem: A meter has a seal on it. What should an electrician do about the seal?
options: Cut it to check the meter connections
Replace it with a new cable tie after the work is done
Remove it if the customer agrees
Never break it; only the power company may

questions.stem: In a standard meter socket, where are the terminals for the incoming supply?
options: At the top of the socket
At the bottom of the socket
On the neutral bar only
On the earth terminal only

questions.stem: How should a meter socket be fixed to the wall?
options: Tilted forward slightly so that rain runs off it
Plumb, level and firm, at the required height
As low as possible so it is easy to read
Loosely, so it can move when the wall expands

questions.stem: Where should a meter socket normally be placed?
options: Inside the house in a locked bedroom
Behind the water tank at the back of the yard
Outside, where the power company can reach it
Under the kitchen sink, out of sight

questions.stem: Which fitting should be used where conduit enters the top of an outdoor meter socket?
options: An open bushing with no seal
Any plastic fitting from the shop
A wooden plug with a hole in it
A rainproof (watertight) hub

questions.stem: In a distribution panel, what is the busbar?
options: The steel bar that holds the panel to the wall stud
The cover that hides the breakers
The metal bar that carries current to the breakers
The label that lists the circuits

questions.stem: In a 110 V / 220 V panel, which breaker is used for a 220 V circuit such as a water heater?
options: A double-pole breaker
A single-pole breaker
A GFCI socket outlet
A plug-in fuse

questions.stem: How do you decide the rating of the breaker for a circuit?
options: Use the largest breaker that will fit in the panel slot
Use the same rating as the main breaker
Use the smallest breaker in the box
Match it to the load and the cable it protects

questions.stem: Why should circuits be shared evenly between the two lines in the panel?
options: So the panel looks neat and tidy
To balance the load on the supply
So that fewer breakers are needed overall
To make the meter read less

questions.stem: Where are the neutral and the earth joined together in a building's installation?
options: At every socket outlet in the building
At each light switch box
At the main service position only
At every sub-panel in the building

questions.stem: In a sub-panel fed from the main panel, how are the neutral and earth bars arranged?
options: Kept separate, with no bond between them
Joined with a link, like the main panel
Both connected to the water pipe only
Neutral bar removed and earth used instead

questions.stem: What is the job of the main breaker in a distribution panel?
options: To switch on just one of the light circuits
To switch off and protect the whole panel
To measure how much power the house uses
To join the neutral to the earth rod

questions.stem: A knockout was removed from a panel by mistake. What should be done with the opening?
options: Leave it open so air can flow and cool the panel
Cover it over with insulating tape
Stuff it with paper
Close it with a proper blanking cap

questions.stem: Why are connectors or bushings fitted where cables enter a panel?
options: To make the panel easier to lift
To stop lizards and insects nesting in the panel
To protect the cable and hold it firmly
To earth the neutral conductor

questions.stem: Why must panel terminals be tightened to the maker's torque?
options: A loose joint can overheat and cause a fire
So that the breaker trips more quickly on a fault
So the panel cover fits better
So the meter reads correctly

questions.stem: Aluminium conductors are to be connected in a panel. What should you check?
options: That they are painted to stop rust
That they are joined to copper by twisting
That they are tinned with solder first
That the terminals are rated for aluminium

questions.stem: What should be written on the panel's circuit schedule (directory)?
options: The date the panel was bought
What each breaker supplies
The name of the inspector
The price of each breaker

questions.stem: The main conductors from the meter socket to the main breaker must be sized for what?
options: The smallest breaker in the panel
The size of the meter socket box and its cover
The rating of the main breaker and service
The number of light points

questions.stem: Why should the main conductors from the meter to the panel be as short as is practical?
options: Less voltage drop and less to go wrong
So the meter reads a lower bill
So that the power company can see them clearly
So that no conduit is needed

questions.stem: How are the main conductors between an outdoor meter socket and the panel usually protected?
options: Tied to the wall with wire
Run inside suitable conduit
Left loose so they can be checked
Wrapped in insulating tape

questions.stem: What is the main job of the meter earthing (grounding) system?
options: To make the meter spin more slowly
To carry the normal neutral current every day
To keep the panel cool in hot weather
To give fault currents a safe path to earth

questions.stem: Which of these makes a good earth electrode for a house?
options: A metal rod driven deep into moist ground
A length of plastic water pipe buried in the yard
The metal roof sheets of the house
The gas pipe that feeds the stove

questions.stem: How should an earth rod be driven into the ground?
options: Only half way in, so it can be pulled out later
Into dry gravel under the house floor slab
Fully, so the top is at or below ground level
At an angle into the concrete path

questions.stem: How should the earthing conductor be connected to the earth rod?
options: Twisted tightly round the rod and taped over
Soldered to the top of the rod
Pushed into the soil next to the rod
With an approved earth clamp, tightened well

questions.stem: The earthing conductor runs down an outside wall to the rod. Where it could be hit or damaged, what should be done?
options: Nothing; it is only an earth wire
Protect it with conduit or a cover
Paint it the same colour as the wall
Bury it in the wall plaster loosely

questions.stem: Which instrument measures the resistance of an earth electrode?
options: An earth resistance tester
A voltage tester
A test lamp on the neutral bar
A low-resistance ohmmeter only

questions.stem: An earth electrode test gives a reading that is too high. What is usually done?
options: Paint the rod with copper paint
Wrap the rod in plastic to keep it dry
Drive more rods, spaced apart and bonded
Disconnect the rod and use the water pipe

questions.stem: Why can an earth electrode reading be higher in the dry season?
options: The rod grows longer in the heat
The meter uses more power
The clamp gets tighter in the sun
Dry soil does not conduct as well

questions.stem: Why are metal water pipes bonded to the main earthing terminal?
options: To stop the water from getting hot
So they cannot reach a dangerous voltage
So the water pressure stays steady
To use them in place of the neutral conductor

questions.stem: Before you work inside an existing distribution panel, what must you do?
options: Switch off only the breakers you will touch
Work carefully with one hand behind your back
Switch off, lock off, tag and prove it dead
Wear rubber boots and work on it live

questions.stem: The main breaker in a house panel is switched off. Which part can still be live?
options: The incoming conductors and main breaker terminals
The outgoing terminals of every branch circuit breaker
The cables to the lights and sockets
The panel's door and its hinges

questions.stem: The main conductors between the meter and the main breaker must be worked on. How are they made dead?
options: By switching off the main breaker
By switching off all the branch breakers in the panel
By removing the panel cover
The power company disconnects the supply

questions.stem: Why do you check a voltage tester on a known live source before you prove a panel dead?
options: To warm up the tester
To be sure the tester is working
To reset the tester's display before you use it
To discharge the panel

questions.stem: Before a new installation is connected, which tests are done with it dead?
options: Earth fault loop and RCD trip tests
Only a check that every light comes on when switched
Continuity, insulation resistance and polarity
Voltage and current at each socket

questions.stem: Before an insulation resistance test on a new installation, what should be done with any electronic equipment connected to it?
options: Disconnect it so that it is not damaged
Leave it connected to test it too
Switch it on so it reads correctly
Cover it with a dry cloth to protect it

questions.stem: In Jamaica, what must happen before the power company will connect a new installation?
options: The customer pays the first month's bill
It passes the government electrical inspection
The electrician fits and signs the meter seal
The panel and its cover are painted to match the wall

questions.stem: Why must the area in front of a distribution panel be kept clear?
options: So the panel stays cool in summer
So the meter reader can park a vehicle right there
So paint can dry on the wall
So it can be reached and worked on safely

questions.stem: Which is the most suitable place to mount a distribution panel in a house?
options: Inside a shower room
Above the kitchen stove
In a dry, easy-to-reach place inside
Inside a clothes closet behind the clothes

questions.stem: Which colour is commonly used for earth (grounding) conductors in a panel?
options: Green, green-yellow or bare copper
Black or red, like the line conductors
White or grey, the same as the neutral
Blue or brown, as on the old cables

questions.stem: Which tool tightens breaker and busbar terminal screws to the maker's value?
options: A hammer
Slip-joint pliers with long handles
An adjustable spanner
A torque screwdriver

questions.stem: When the panel work is finished, what should be left with the customer?
options: The spare breakers, still in their boxes
The circuit schedule and test record
The keys to the meter socket and its seal
The old cable off-cuts, for future use

questions.stem: After installing a panel, why must all wire off-cuts and metal filings be removed from inside it?
options: So the panel weighs less
So the inspector can count the parts used
They could cause a short circuit
They are needed for the next job

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the overhead cables that run from the power company's pole to the building?
What is the name of the cap at the top of the service pipe that stops rain getting in where the supply cables enter?
What is the frequency of the mains supply in Jamaica, in hertz?
What is the name of the conductor or screw that joins the neutral bar to the earth bar at the main service position?
On a ring-type meter socket, what is the name of the metal ring that holds the meter in place and takes the seal?
A common earth rod is made of steel with a thin coating of another metal. Which metal is the coating?
What do the letters GFCI stand for?
What is the name of the paste put on aluminium conductors before termination, to stop an oxide layer forming?
A water heater is rated 3300 W at 220 V. What current does it draw, in amperes?
In what unit is the cross-section (size) of a metric conductor given?
In what unit does an electricity meter record the energy used?
What is the name of the small box set in the ground over the top of an earth rod, so that the clamp can be inspected?
Which instrument is clamped around a conductor to measure the current without disconnecting it?
What is the name of the flexible steel tape used to pull conductors through conduit?
What is the name of the device fitted at a panel to protect equipment from voltage spikes, such as those caused by lightning?

essays.stem: Explain why an electrician must never work on the power company's side of the meter, and which parts can still be live when the main breaker is switched off.
essays.modelAnswer: The service drop, the meter and the supply (line) side of the meter socket are under the power company's control. They come straight from the power company's lines, so there is no breaker or fuse in the building that can switch them off, and a fault there can give a very large current, a bad shock or a flash burn. Only the power company may connect or disconnect the supply, remove or fit the meter, or break the meter seal. When the main breaker in the panel is switched off, only the circuits after it are off. The incoming conductors from the meter (the terminal mains) and the incoming terminals of the main breaker are still live. An electrician must keep clear of them and keep their cover or barrier in place. If they must be worked on, the power company is asked to disconnect the supply first, and the electrician still proves them dead before touching.
markingPoints: The supply side comes straight from the power company with no protection in the building that can switch it off
Only the power company connects or disconnects the supply, or fits the meter; the seal is never broken
With the main breaker off, the incoming conductors and main breaker incoming terminals are still live
Keeps clear of these parts and keeps covers or barriers in place
Asks the power company to disconnect, then still proves dead before work

essays.stem: Describe how you would install a new meter socket on the outside wall of a house before the supply is connected.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would check the power company's rules and the drawing for the type of meter socket, its height and its place on the wall, where the power company can reach it and it is not blocked by gates, tanks or plants. I would make sure there is no supply anywhere near the work. I would mark the position, check it with a spirit level and fix the socket plumb and level with fixings that suit the wall, so it is firm. I would remove only the knockouts that are needed and fit rainproof hubs at the top and suitable connectors below, so water cannot get in. I would run the conduit from the socket to the panel and bring in the earthing conductor as the drawing shows. The supply (line) terminals and the meter are the power company's part, so I would not connect any supply to them. Finally I would fit the cover, check everything is tight and record the work.
markingPoints: Checks the power company's rules and drawing for type, height and an easy-to-reach position
Fixes the socket plumb, level and firm
Uses only the knockouts needed, with rainproof hubs and connectors
Runs conduit to the panel and brings in the earthing conductor
Leaves the supply terminals and the meter to the power company

essays.stem: Describe how you would choose a place for a distribution panel and mount it ready for wiring.
essays.modelAnswer: I would choose a place inside the house that is dry, cool and easy to reach, such as a hallway or utility room, not a bathroom, a closet full of clothes or a place over the stove. It should be close to the meter so that the main conductors are short, and there must be a clear space in front so a person can stand and work safely. I would check the drawing for the height, then mark the position and use a spirit level. I would fix the panel firmly with screws or anchors that suit the wall, keeping it plumb and level. I would plan the cable and conduit entries, and remove only the knockouts I need, fitting connectors or bushings so cables are protected and held. Any knockout removed by mistake would be closed with a blanking cap. Before wiring, I would check that the busbars, neutral bar and earth bar are clean, tight and as the maker supplied them.
markingPoints: Chooses a dry, cool, easy-to-reach place, not a bathroom, closet or above a stove
Close to the meter, with clear working space in front
Fixes it firmly, plumb and level, at the height on the drawing
Removes only the knockouts needed and fits connectors or bushings; blanks any mistakes
Checks busbars and neutral and earth bars before wiring

essays.stem: Describe how you would install the main conductors (terminal mains) between the meter socket and the main breaker of the panel, before the supply is connected.
essays.modelAnswer: I would check the drawing and the size of the service, and choose conductors sized for the main breaker rating and the length of run, as the code and the tables require. I would run suitable conduit between the meter socket and the panel, as short and direct as practical, with rainproof fittings outside and bushings where it enters the boxes. I would pull in the two line conductors, the neutral and the earth, using colours or markings that show which is which, without damaging the insulation. At the panel end I would strip each conductor to the right length and connect the lines to the main breaker, the neutral to the neutral bar and the earth to the earth bar. If the conductors are aluminium, I would use terminals rated for aluminium and anti-oxidant compound. I would tighten every terminal to the maker's torque. At the meter socket I would connect only the load terminals; the supply side is for the power company. Finally I would test and record the work.
markingPoints: Sizes conductors for the main breaker rating and run length from the tables
Runs conduit short and direct, with rainproof fittings and bushings
Identifies the lines, neutral and earth clearly and pulls in without damage
Connects correctly at the panel, with aluminium-rated terminals and compound if aluminium, tightened to torque
Connects only the load terminals at the meter socket; supply side left to the power company

essays.stem: Explain how you would connect the branch circuits inside a new distribution panel.
essays.modelAnswer: With the panel not connected to any supply, I would read the circuit list and choose a breaker for each circuit, matched to the load and the cable it protects. A single-pole breaker is used for 110 V circuits such as lights and sockets, and a double-pole breaker for 220 V circuits such as a water heater or an air conditioner. I would place the breakers so that the load is shared evenly between the two lines. I would bring each cable in through a connector, strip the sheath inside the panel and dress the conductors neatly along the sides. The line conductor goes to its breaker, the neutral to the neutral bar and the earth to the earth bar, one conductor to each terminal unless the maker allows more. Every terminal is tightened to the maker's torque. I would fill in the circuit schedule, saying what each breaker supplies, and close any spare spaces in the cover with blanks.
markingPoints: Matches each breaker to its load and cable
Single-pole for 110 V circuits, double-pole for 220 V circuits
Balances the load between the two lines
Connects line, neutral and earth to the right places, neatly, tightened to torque
Fills in the circuit schedule and blanks spare spaces

essays.stem: Explain why a meter earthing system is needed, and describe how you would install the earth rod and earthing conductor.
essays.modelAnswer: The earthing system connects the installation to the general mass of earth. It gives fault and lightning currents a safe path, keeps metal parts near earth potential and helps the protective devices work. Before driving the rod, I would check the site plan and ask about buried cables, water pipes and septic tanks so that none are hit. I would place the rod in moist soil, at the distance from the building that the rules and drawing require. I would drive the rod in fully so the top is at or below ground level, or in an inspection pit, wearing safety glasses, gloves and boots. I would fix the earthing conductor to the rod with an approved clamp and tighten it well, leaving the clamp where it can be inspected. I would run the conductor in one length, without joins, to the main earthing terminal, protecting it with conduit where it could be damaged. Finally I would test the earth electrode resistance and record the result.
markingPoints: Explains the purpose: safe path for fault and lightning currents, keeps metal near earth potential
Checks for buried services before driving the rod
Drives the rod fully in moist soil, with PPE
Approved clamp, tight and able to be inspected; conductor in one length to the main earthing terminal
Protects the conductor where it could be damaged and tests the electrode resistance

essays.stem: Explain why the neutral and earth are joined at the main service position only, and why they are kept separate in a sub-panel.
essays.modelAnswer: In normal use, the neutral carries current back to the supply, but the earth conductors should carry current only when there is a fault. At the main service position, a bonding jumper joins the neutral to the earth so that a fault to a metal part has a low-resistance path back to the supply, and the breaker trips quickly. If the neutral and earth were joined again at a sub-panel or a socket, some of the normal neutral current would flow along the earth conductors, the metal conduit, the panel cases and the water pipes. These metal parts could then carry a voltage and give a shock, and the current could cause heat, interference and trips on GFCI devices. So in a sub-panel the neutral bar is insulated from the case and the earth bar is bonded to the case, and the sub-panel is fed with separate neutral and earth conductors. This keeps normal current in the neutral only.
markingPoints: Neutral carries normal current; earth carries current only in a fault
One bond at the main service gives a low-resistance fault path so the breaker trips
Extra bonds let neutral current flow on earth conductors and metal parts
This can cause shock risk, heat, interference or GFCI trips
Sub-panel: neutral bar insulated, earth bar bonded to the case, fed by separate neutral and earth

essays.stem: A new circuit must be added to an existing house panel. Describe how you would isolate the panel safely, and what you must remember about the parts that stay live.
essays.modelAnswer: I would tell the household that the power will be off. I would switch off the main breaker, fit a lock to it so nobody can switch it on, and fix a tag with my name, the date and the reason, keeping the key. I would check my voltage tester on a known live source or a proving unit, then test at the busbars and the outgoing side of the main breaker, line to line, each line to neutral and each line to earth, to prove them dead. Then I would check the tester again on the known source. I must remember that the incoming conductors from the meter and the incoming terminals of the main breaker are still live, because they come straight from the power company. I would keep their barrier or cover in place and keep my hands and tools well away. If my work means touching or coming close to them, I must not go on; the power company must disconnect the supply first. I would never work live, and I would follow the Centre's rules.
markingPoints: Warns the household; switches off the main breaker, locks off and tags
Checks the tester on a known live source or proving unit before testing
Proves dead at the busbars and outgoing side between all conductors, then checks the tester again
Knows the incoming conductors and main breaker incoming terminals stay live; keeps barriers in place and keeps clear
Stops and asks the power company to disconnect if work is needed near the incoming side; never works live

essays.stem: Describe the inspection and tests you would carry out on a new panel and meter position before asking for the government inspection.
essays.modelAnswer: All tests are done with the installation dead and not connected to the supply. First I would inspect by eye: the meter socket and panel are fixed firmly, the right breakers are fitted, conductors are the right size and colour, terminals are tight, there is only one neutral-earth bond at the main service position, knockouts are closed, connectors and bushings are fitted, the earthing conductor and clamp are in place, and the circuit schedule is filled in. Then I would do the dead tests in the usual order. First the continuity of the protective conductors and bonding, using a low-resistance ohmmeter, to show every earth path is unbroken. Then insulation resistance between the conductors and to earth, after disconnecting any electronic equipment. Then polarity, to show that breakers and switches are in the line conductor and connections are correct. I would also test the earth electrode resistance. I would record all the results and put right any fault before asking for the inspection.
markingPoints: Installation dead and not connected during the tests
Visual inspection of fixings, breakers, conductors, terminals, single neutral-earth bond, closures and schedule
Continuity of protective conductors and bonding first
Insulation resistance (electronic equipment disconnected), then polarity
Earth electrode test, results recorded and faults put right

essays.stem: Describe how you would finish, clean up and hand over the job after installing a panel and meter socket.
essays.modelAnswer: When the tests are done and all faults are put right, I would make sure every cover, blank and door is fitted and closed, and that the earthing clamp and inspection pit are left tidy and able to be inspected. I would check that the circuit schedule is complete and easy to read, with every breaker labelled. I would remove all wire off-cuts, strips of insulation and metal filings from inside the panel and the meter socket, because loose pieces could cause a short circuit. I would sweep up, sort the waste into the right bins and return the tools and spare materials, reporting any damaged tools. Then I would complete the paperwork: the test results, any changes to the drawing, and the forms needed for the government inspection. I would explain to the customer where the main breaker is and how to switch off in an emergency, and that the power company will connect the supply and fit the meter after the inspection is passed.
markingPoints: Covers, blanks and doors fitted; earthing clamp left able to be inspected
Circuit schedule complete and every breaker labelled
Off-cuts and filings removed from panel and meter socket; area cleaned and waste sorted
Test results, drawing changes and inspection forms completed
Explains the main breaker to the customer and that the power company connects after inspection

practical1.title: Mount a meter socket and distribution panel and install the terminal mains on a training board
practical1.brief: As a group, mount a meter socket and a distribution panel on the training board, as shown on the instructor's drawing. Run conduit between them and install the main conductors (terminal mains) from the load terminals of the meter socket to the main breaker, the neutral bar and the earth bar. The supply (line) terminals of the meter socket are not used: leave them empty and fix a label on them saying "Supply side: power company only". Fit the main breaker, one single-pole and one double-pole branch breaker, connect two short circuit tails, fit the neutral-earth bond only where the instructor shows, and fill in the circuit schedule. Then do the dead tests: continuity of protective conductors, insulation resistance and polarity. The board is never connected to a supply. Every member fixes or connects at least one part and carries out or records one test. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Training board with space for a meter socket and a distribution panel
Ring-type or ringless meter socket (training use, no meter fitted)
Distribution panel with main breaker, one single-pole and one double-pole breaker, neutral and earth bars
Conduit, hubs, connectors and bushings to suit
Main conductors and short circuit tails, sized as on the drawing
Spirit level, drill, screwdrivers, torque screwdriver, cable cutters, strippers, fish tape
Low-resistance ohmmeter and insulation resistance tester
photos: Meter socket and panel fixed, with a spirit level on each
Conduit run between them, with hubs and bushings fitted
The load-side connections in the meter socket, with the supply terminals empty and labelled
The main conductors connected at the main breaker, neutral bar and earth bar
The branch breakers and circuit tails connected neatly
The continuity, insulation resistance and polarity test readings
The completed circuit schedule, covers fitted, area cleaned
checklist: Fixed the meter socket and panel plumb, level and firm
Removed only the knockouts needed and fitted hubs, connectors and bushings
Connected only the load side of the meter socket and labelled the supply side
Connected lines, neutral and earth to the correct places, tightened to torque
Chose single-pole and double-pole breakers correctly and balanced the lines
Carried out or recorded the dead tests in the right order
Filled in the circuit schedule clearly
Removed all off-cuts from the enclosures and left the area clean
safety: The training board is never connected to a supply during this task
No work on the supply side of the meter socket; it stays empty and labelled
Wear safety glasses when drilling and cutting; keep fingers clear of cutter blades
Warn everyone before an insulation resistance test and do not touch the conductors during it
Follow the makers' instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Install and test a meter earthing system with an earth rod and bonding
practical2.brief: As a group, install a meter earthing system in the Centre's earthing practice area. Check the site plan with the instructor for buried services, then drive an earth rod fully into the ground (or into an inspection pit), fix the earthing conductor to it with an approved clamp, and run the conductor in one length, protected by conduit where shown, to the main earthing terminal on the training board. Bond a length of metal water pipe on the board to the main earthing terminal. Test the continuity of the earthing and bonding conductors, and measure the earth electrode resistance with the earth resistance tester as the instructor shows. Record all results. The training board is not connected to a supply. Every member takes a turn at driving the rod, fixing the clamp or conductor, and doing or recording a test. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Copper-clad steel earth rod and approved earth clamp
Copper earthing conductor and conduit with saddles
Main earthing terminal on the training board and a short length of metal water pipe with a bonding clamp
Sledgehammer with a driving head, or a rod driver as the Centre provides
Earth resistance tester with its test spikes and leads
photos: The site plan checked for buried services, and the rod position marked
The rod being driven, with every member in PPE
The rod top at or below ground level, with the clamp fitted
The earthing conductor run in conduit to the main earthing terminal
The bonding clamp on the water pipe, with its label
The earth resistance tester set up, and its reading
The results sheet and the area tidied
checklist: Checked for buried services before driving the rod
Wore safety glasses, gloves and boots and used the driving tool safely
Drove the rod fully and fixed the clamp tight, able to be inspected
Ran the earthing conductor in one length, protected where needed
Fitted the bonding clamp to the water pipe and labelled it
Carried out or recorded the continuity and earth electrode tests correctly
Explained what to do if the earth reading is too high
Left the area tidy and returned all tools
safety: Check for buried cables and pipes before driving the rod
Wear safety glasses, gloves and boots; keep others well clear of the hammer
Use a driving head on the rod; never hold the rod top with your hand while it is struck
Keep people and animals clear of the test spikes and leads during the earth test
The training board is not connected to a supply; follow the tester maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
